newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures end steady-higher, bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures end steady-higher, bellies mixed.

text.p: Nearby CME live hog futures closed steady while deferred contracts were slightly higher.
Hog futures fell sharply last week erasing the futures-to-cash premium, traders noted. Now futures are at a slight discount to cash, which offered light support.
October hogs closed at 52.425 cents per lb versus top cash prices of $55.50 per cwt in Iowa and $54.00 in Illinois.
Ample hog marketings last week and Tuesday kept cash prices under pressure and fueled selling in the futures. USDA estimated Tuesday's slaughter at 366,000 head versus 350,000 a year ago.
Because of the U.S. Labor day holiday this week, a week ago comparison was not valid.

Pork belly contracts were mixed with february and March 1997 contracts ending lower and deferreds higher. A sharp break in cash belly prices last week motivated selling of the nearby futures Tuesday, traders said.
A sharp drop in cash belly prices last week weighed on futures. Analysts attributed the drop in cash prices to a slowdown in retail bacon use and a rise in production.
USDA quoted 12- to 14-lb cash belly prices at $68.00 per cwt in the 1115 CDT carlot pork report Tuesday versus $69.00 to $70.00 quoted in the same report Friday.
Late local short covering trimmed losses in the February and March 1997 pork bellies, which were sharply lower early.
Hogs closed unchanged to up 0.425 cent with October unchanged at 52.425 cents per lb. Pork bellies were down 0.900 cent to up 1.300 cents with February off the most at 77.150 cents per lb.
